title: Slack MCP Server | Awesome MCP Servers

facts.fact: The slack-mcp server provides 21+ tools for Slack interaction, according to the page.
facts.quote: It provides 21+ tools for comprehensive Slack interaction:

facts.fact: The page states that the Slack-reading feature 'List unread direct messages with read markers' works only with browser-session auth and uses Slack's client.counts endpoint, which is not part of the public Web API.
facts.quote: List unread direct messages with read markers (browser-session auth only; uses Slack's `client.counts` endpoint, which is not part of the public Web API)

facts.fact: The page lists these OAuth scopes for the bot-token setup: channels:read, channels:history, channels:manage, groups:read, groups:history, groups:write, chat:write, reactions:read, reactions:write, search:read, users:read, commands, mpim:write.
When SLACK_BOT_TOKEN and SLACK_XOXC_TOKEN/SLACK_XOXD_TOKEN are both set, the bot token takes precedence.
facts.quote: If both `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and `SLACK_XOXC_TOKEN`/`SLACK_XOXD_TOKEN` are set, the bot token takes precedence.

facts.fact: LOGS_CHANNEL_ID is optional; when it is omitted, tool activity is written to stderr instead of being posted to Slack.
facts.quote: `LOGS_CHANNEL_ID` is optional. When omitted, tool activity is written to **stderr** instead of posted to Slack.

facts.fact: Read-only mode is enabled by setting SLACK_MCP_READ_ONLY to a truthy value of 1, true, yes, or on (case-insensitive), or by passing --read-only at startup.
facts.quote: set `SLACK_MCP_READ_ONLY` to a truthy value (`1`, `true`, `yes`, or `on`, case-insensitive).

facts.fact: In read-only mode, the tools post_message, send_dm, post_command, add_reaction, and join_channel raise an error.
facts.quote: tools that mutate Slack state (`post_message`, `send_dm`, `post_command`, `add_reaction`, `join_channel`) raise a clear error.

facts.fact: The setup script's --refresh-tokens flag re-extracts tokens when they expire and skips all other setup steps.
facts.quote: Re-extract tokens when they expire (skips all other steps)

facts.fact: The Linux desktop-app token refresh script requires python3, python3-cryptography, secret-tool (libsecret/gnome-keyring), curl, and jq.
By default, the desktop-app token refresh script writes tokens to ~/.local/share/slack-mcp/tokens.env.
The page states that this is not an official Red Hat tool.
facts.quote: Disclaimer: This is not an official Red Hat tool.

facts.fact: The page gives two setup-script URLs that point to different GitHub organizations: one under redhat-ai-tools (the listing's GitHub link) and one under redhat-community-ai-tools (the setup script).
